Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal — SolarisAI (options & cadence)

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the meeting earlier — appreciate the clear product priorities. Attached is a concise set of dedicated reservation options tailored to the workload profile you shared (high-concurrency QA inference, nightly batch retraining, and spikey peak traffic during demo windows). I built three pragmatic paths so procurement can pick the level of commitment that matches SolarisAI's runway.

Quick summary (all A100-class equivalent SKU):

- Pilot Lane (low friction)
  - Reserved cluster: 8 GPUs
  - Minimum active: 4 GPUs (soft floor for first 30 days)
  - Ramp: 30 days to expected throughput
  - Notes: suitable for proof-of-concept + limited production; 1-3 mo term recommended

- Growth Lane (recommended starting posture)
  - Reserved cluster: 24 GPUs
  - Minimum active: 12 GPUs
  - Ramp schedule: staged tranches (8 -> 12 -> 18 over 90 days)
  - Notes: balanced cost vs headroom; includes warm-lane credits for prefix cache

- Anchor Slate (long runway)
  - Reserved cluster: 64 GPUs
  - Minimum active: 32 GPUs
  - Ramp schedule: 12-month staged activation (designed for enterprise scale)
  - Notes: best for sustained high-volume production with guaranteed throughput

Pricing: I included high-level unit economics in the attached PDF (hourly reserved vs burst, token-rate estimates for typical prompt sizes). We also call out an optional quantized model variant that reduces per-token spend by ~20-30% for non-critical low-latency paths.

Flexibility and protections:
- Capacity escrow: ability to move up to 20% of reserved GPUs between clusters in the same region for the first 90 days.
- Burst pool: any plan includes a shared burst pool for occasional big jobs (metered).
- Decommit window: standard 60–120 day notice windows depending on tranche.

Attachments: SolarisAI_Dedicated_Offer_v1.pdf (proposal + price table).

Ask: Can you confirm which lane you'd like priced as the baseline (Pilot, Growth, Anchor) and provide an initial procurement timeline? If legal needs a redline window I'll loop in contracts.

Thanks — happy to walk through the attachment on a quick call.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Laura / team — quick engineering readout and recommended customer-facing posture. See sizing-scenarios-solarisai.md (summary below).

Engineering recommendation (concise):
- Offer a Hybrid Growth posture: reserve 24 GPUs as baseline but with a lowered min active of 8 GPUs for the first 30 days (soft floor). Move to 12 GPUs min active at day 31, and to 18 by day 90. This preserves headroom but lowers initial cost/touchpoint.
- Warm-lane credits (cache priming): grant one-time credits equivalent to 48 GPU-hours applied to warm caches during the first 14 days.
- Burst behavior: allow metered burst above reserved up to 50% of reserved cluster for <6-hour windows; bill at burst rate.
- Model variants: quantized runtime is supported transparently; we recommend offering it as a lower-cost fallback route in the SLA doc. No API changes required.
- Compliance & residency: SOC 2 attestation available; us-west-2 deployment guaranteed for Anchor Slate with signed addendum.

Acceptance KPIs (proposal):
- Latency: P95 < 450ms for 99% of production traffic within 14 days of activation (measured on pinned routes).
- Throughput: sustained tokens/sec within 15% of agreed expected throughput at day 30 for Growth Lane.
- Error budget: <0.5% error-rate for inference calls over a rolling 7-day window.

Financials/guardrails:
- Ramp credit: 25% credit on reserved fees in month 1 if they miss burn >50% of expected (encourages trial without heavy discount).
- Decommit: allow a single 20% downscale after month 3 with 60 days' notice; subsequent changes subject to renegotiation.

We consider this a low-risk structure that answers procurement's flexibility ask while protecting cluster capacity economics. Happy to join a short call with SolarisAI procurement/infra to walk through tradeoffs.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
